hints.title: Sorted Array Boundary
hints.text: Sort the array to quickly locate elements strictly greater than any given value.

hints.title: Upper Bound Search
hints.text: Use binary search (upper bound) to find the first element in sorted array strictly greater than x.

hints.title: Threshold Filtering
hints.text: The count of strictly greater elements is n - upper_bound_index. Check if this count is at least k.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def countElementsWithKGreater(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        sorted_nums = sorted(nums)
        n = len(nums)
        count = 0
        for x in nums:
            # First element strictly greater than x
            idx = bisect.bisect_right(sorted_nums, x)
            strictly_greater = n - idx
            if strictly_greater >= k:
                count += 1
        return count
```

complexity.notes: Sorting followed by binary search upper bound per element.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Counting greater elements by full linear scan per item costs quadratic O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(N) memory for sorted array copy.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Sort and use binary search upper bound to count strictly greater elements in logarithmic time.
